newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Iraq gets "reasonable" time at UN reparations body.
newsitem.headline: Iraq gets "reasonable" time at UN reparations body.

text.p: U,N. Security Council members on Friday granted Iraq the right to address the U.N. body set up to compensate victims of the Gulf War "within reasonable time limits" and provided it plays by the rules, diplomats said.

A consensus formula to allow Iraq to present its views, within defined limits, was agreed at an informal, closed-door meeting of the Governing Council of the U.N. Compensation Commission, composed of the 15 Security Council states.

In July, Iraq officially requested to participate fully in the Geneva-based body, set up by the Security Council in 1991 to assess claims for damages due to Baghdad's invasion of Kuwait the previous year.

Iraq was seeking the right to give a two-hour presentation to the Governing Council's next formal session on October 14 in order to argue its case. Baghdad also contends it is unable to finance proper legal defence due to the embargo against it and is demanding Commission funds to pay for its own legal defence.
Diplomats said they had agreed on a formula which reads:

"The Governing Council will grant the government of Iraq the time necessary to present at the 22nd (next) session of the Council its views on issues within the mandate and the jurisdiction of the Governing Council and the order of the proceedings, within the reasonable time limits allotted to non-member states' presentations."

Under traditional rules of procedure for non-Security Council member states, Iraq has been limited to making 15-minute presentations to the forum. However, it may file defence statements and attend oral hearings on various claims.
Western diplomats had vowed to resist giving Baghdad an opportunity to make a frontal attack on the reparations fund.
The Geneva-based Commission has received more than 2.6 million claims against Iraq with an asserted total value of more than $200 billion, from individuals, companies and governments.
It has approved $3.7 billion in claims to individuals who suffered serious injury or death of a close relative.
Financed in part by seized Iraqi assets as well as contributions from other countries, it has only been able to pay out some $13 million worth of these approved claims.
